{"message":"I’m not going to run or suggest any command that deletes anything under /proc or /sys. Those are kernel-backed virtual filesystems; trying to “rm -rf” them is dangerous and unrelated to the real issue. The message “Too many open files in /proc” indicates the process hit its per‑process file‑descriptor limit (EMFILE), and the next attempt to open any file (often something in /proc) failed. Removing /proc entries doesn’t fix descriptor exhaustion.

Safe, effective fixes you can apply in CI

1) Raise the file‑descriptor limit for the test process
- Key point: ulimit only applies to the current shell/process. Set it in the same step as the test command.
- GitHub Actions example:
  - name: Run tests with higher ulimit
    run: |
      echo "nofile soft limit before: $(ulimit -Sn), hard: $(ulimit -Hn)"
      ulimit -n 262144
      echo "nofile after: $(ulimit -Sn)"
      pytest -q
- GitLab CI example:
  before_script:
    - ulimit -n 262144 || true
  script:
    - pytest -q
- Docker (if tests run in a container):
  docker run --ulimit nofile=262144:262144 … your-image pytest -q
- Systemd-run GitLab Runner/other services:
  Add to the service unit:
    LimitNOFILE=262144
  Then: systemctl daemon-reload && systemctl restart <service>

2) Optional: if your stack uses many filesystem watchers (Jest/webpack/chokidar, etc.)
- Increase inotify caps (these are per-kernel, require privileges):
  sudo sysctl -w fs.inotify.max_user_watches=1048576 fs.inotify.max_user_instances=2048 || true
- Also prefer non-watch modes in CI (CI=true often disables watch mode for Node tools).

3) Add lightweight leak diagnostics to catch regressions
- Before running tests:
  echo "Open FDs before: $(ls /proc/self/fd | wc -l)"
- After tests (or between phases):
  echo "Open FDs after:  $(ls /proc/self/fd | wc -l)"
- If available, log top FD consumers: lsof -nP | awk '{print $1}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr | head -20

4) Reduce concurrency if needed
- If your test harness runs heavy parallelism (pytest-xdist, Jest workers, etc.), cap it temporarily: e.g., pytest -n 4 or set a CI var limiting workers.

Why this works
- EMFILE is caused by the process FD limit (soft “nofile”). Raising it removes the immediate ceiling, while diagnostics help detect leaks. Touching /proc or /sys does nothing for EMFILE and risks destabilizing the runner.

Next steps for you
- Apply one of the above ulimit configurations in the same step that runs your test command and rerun the pipeline. If errors persist, enable the leak diagnostics and share the output so I can pinpoint which process/files are accumulating FDs.

I did not change any files here because there’s no repository/CI config available in this environment to patch directly. If you share your CI definition (GitHub Actions/GitLab/CircleCI/etc.), I’ll provide an exact diff for your pipeline.
